candidates.title: Sintilimab plus CAPOX induction versus consolidation around SCRT in pMMR/MSS LARC
candidates.sourceLevel: Original protocol full text reviewed; no clinical results.
candidates.reason: Planned 36 patients; both groups contain sintilimab+CAPOX and 30 Gy/6 fractions. No immunotherapy-free comparator, efficacy or safety outcomes. Retrospective registration June 2025 after first enrollment December 2024. Do not treat design hypotheses as results.

candidates.title: CREATE versus conventional double-stapling for ultralow rectal cancer
candidates.sourceLevel: Original PubMed abstract retrieved via EFetch; complete publisher article unavailable through attempted routes.
candidates.reason: Retrospective multicenter PSM: 448 eligible, 168 matched (60 CREATE/108 conventional). Functional analysis restricted to stoma reversal and completed LARS questionnaires; exact timepoint denominators and full safety need verification. Early LARS association does not establish oncological noninferiority; no significant 24-month LARS difference.

candidates.title: Laparoscopic versus open sphincter-preserving rectal surgery: Fudan retrospective PSM cohort
candidates.sourceLevel: Publisher article and reference PDF reviewed; unresolved internal denominators.
candidates.reason: Historical August 12 first publication, not a new November readout. 9405 selected and 7738 matched (open4993/laparoscopic2745); main text and tables contain conflicting complication/mortality and temporary-stoma counts, denominators and percentages. Do not silently repair or curate numbers until reconciled. Anatomical sphincter preservation is not preserved continence or absence of LARS. Single-center retrospective association with temporal confounding and unequal followup.

candidates.title: CTRI/2021/05/033642: TNT versus conventional CRT interim randomized trial
candidates.sourceLevel: Original PubMed abstract screened; full paper not reviewed this run.
candidates.reason: Historical February 2026 publication surfaced by metadata update. 172 randomized (87/85), interim analysis150 (75/75). No primary pCR difference; exact pCR denominator, full safety and interim analysis plan require full-text verification before inclusion. Do not promote secondary 1-year distant-metastasis finding to mature survival superiority.

candidates.title: EUREKA AI-assisted dissection line selection
candidates.decision: Exclude from clinical-outcome evidence: six scenes,20 surgeons,480 simulated evaluations; no patient-outcome comparison. PubMed primary abstract verified, full text unavailable; fixed-order learning/recall limitation.

candidates.title: Cardiff November12 business update
candidates.decision: Unresolved primary-page access; search-index lead suggests ongoing onvansertib randomized phaseII, not verified new clinical outcomes. No record change.

candidates.title: ATOMIC FDA approval recirculated in November news
candidates.decision: Official FDA confirms October8 approval already represented in ATOMIC record. No new November outcome or new regulatory event; no record change.

correctionScreening.title: Response to targeted therapy or chemotherapy following immunotherapy in patients with gastrointestinal cancers - a case series.
correctionScreening.abstract:
In non-small cell lung cancer, response rates to chemotherapy given after immune checkpoint inhibitors has been reported to be higher compared to response rates to chemotherapy given before immune checkpoint inhibitors. However, this phenomenon has not been reported in patients with gastrointestinal cancers nor with the use of multi-targeted kinase inhibitors.
We present a series of six patients who received multi-targeted kinase inhibitors or chemotherapy after progression on immune checkpoint inhibitors and showed unexpected response. Five of these patients had metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma and received salvage multi-targeted kinase inhibitors. Two of these five patients had no response to initial multi-targeted kinase inhibitors but had unexpected response to re-challenge with multi-targeted kinase inhibitors after immune checkpoint inhibitors exposure. The sixth patient had metastatic rectal cancer and showed response to salvage chemotherapy following immune checkpoint inhibitors.
We postulate that the sequencing of immune checkpoint inhibitors prior to other forms of systemic therapy may potentially lead to an immunomodulatory effect in gastrointestinal cancers with potential improvement in response rates.
